newsitem.title: USA: SEC's Levitt to speak at Connecticut town meeting.
newsitem.headline: SEC's Levitt to speak at Connecticut town meeting.

text.p: Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Arthur Levitt will join two U.S. senators and a banking commissioner on April 14 in hosting an investors' town meeting in Hamden, Conn., the commission said.

"As more Americans put their money in the market, they must be informed and must understand their investment," Levitt said in a statement. "Informed investors are better able to protect themselves against potential fraud and abuse."

Also speaking at the town meeting, to be held at Quinnipiac College, will be Connecticut Democratic Senators Christopher Dodd and Joseph Liberman and Connecticut Banking Commissioner John Burke. The public is invited.
Levitt will offer basic tips to help investors make investment decisions, monitor their investments and avoid problems, the commission said.
Dodd and Lieberman will address issues before Congress that affect individual investors. Burke will describe recent Connecticut investor protection initiatives, SEC said.
The town meeting will run from 0900 EDT/1300 GMT to 1100 EDT/1500 GMT with investment seminars scheduled from 1115 EDT/1515 GMT to 1300 EDT/1700 GMT.
